subject.title: Heartbeat: Use ISO 8601 for Current time and separate trigger timestamp

question: Should OpenClaw change the shared cron-style prompt timestamp contract to ISO 8601 and add a heartbeat trigger timestamp, or keep the current human-readable `Current time` plus `Reference UTC` contract?
rationale: The source path is clear, but this changes a shared model-visible prompt contract and overlaps broader prompt-cache placement work, so automation should not choose the permanent timestamp semantics by itself.

options.title: Adopt shared ISO contract
options.body: Update the shared current-time helper and affected heartbeat, cron, reset, status, and post-compaction tests so model-facing volatile time lines use ISO 8601, then add heartbeat trigger time where wake metadata exists.

options.title: Heartbeat-only trigger field
options.body: Keep shared current-time formatting as-is but add a separate heartbeat wake trigger timestamp for event-driven heartbeats, accepting inconsistent timestamp formats across prompt surfaces.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Preserve the shipped natural-language local `Current time` plus `Reference UTC` contract and narrow or reject the ISO/trigger request.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared ISO contract
recommendation.body: Update the shared current-time helper and affected heartbeat, cron, reset, status, and post-compaction tests so model-facing volatile time lines use ISO 8601, then add heartbeat trigger time where wake metadata exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the shared helper and heartbeat prompt wiring that define the current behavior.
